children: British gilt prices rallied on Thursday, outperforming other major markets as European bonds benefited from a fall in benchmark gas prices, offering a little respite to finance minister John Healey ahead of next month's budget.

Twenty- and 30-year gilt yields, which move inversely to prices and had surged on Tuesday and Wednesday to levels last seen in 1998, fell back to levels seen last week. Short and medium-dated yields remain noticeably higher than the week before.

U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller's remarks that recent progress on inflation could justify keeping rates unchanged, as well as an easing in European front-month benchmark gas prices, contributed to a rally in bonds.
As the market closed, gilt yields across the range of maturities ended up around 8-10 basis points lower on the day.
The 10-year gilt yield (GB10YT=RR) fell by 9 basis points to 5.14%, marking the biggest single-day drop for a month.

The spike in yields seen earlier in the week had raised speculation that it would further erode Healey's margin against the government's self-imposed fiscal rules as he prepares for his first annual budget.
While Healey may be pleased by Thursday's move, Britain's government debt issuance has become increasingly expensive.
Britain sold £900 million ($1.21 billion) of inflation-linked debt on Thursday at the highest real yield in 25 years, highlighting the growing cost of issuing long-dated government bonds.

title: UK gilt prices surge as long-dated yields return to levels seen last week
